answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to a VDF: computing y = x^(2^T) mod N requires T dependent modular squarings, each waiting for the prior result. GPUs may run clone chains concurrently, but cannot parallelize one chain to remove its sequential time bottleneck; more identities therefore require more hardware or elapsed time. A Wesolowski proof lets peers verify completion efficiently. The saffron, timber, and vertex labels do not change this constraint.
